claim: For the Almatroud–Rajagopal–Pham–Grassi system \(\dot x=a_1y^2-a_2z^2,\;\dot y=b_1x^2-b_2z^2,\;\dot z=c_1y^2+c_2z^2-1\) with \(a_1,a_2,b_1,b_2,c_1,c_2>0\), every bounded forward solution has automatically convergent coordinate mean squares, namely \(\lim_{T\to\infty}T^{-1}\int_0^T x^2dt=a_1b_2/[b_1(a_1c_2+a_2c_1)]\), \(\lim_{T\to\infty}T^{-1}\int_0^T y^2dt=a_2/(a_1c_2+a_2c_1)\), and \(\lim_{T\to\infty}T^{-1}\int_0^T z^2dt=a_1/(a_1c_2+a_2c_1)\). Thus all compact invariant probability measures and all periodic orbits have the same coordinate-wise second moments, equal to the squared coordinate magnitudes of the eight equilibria. At the paper's nominal parameters the moments are \(1/8,1/4,1/4\); at its showcased multistable parameter \(c_1=13/5\), both the chaotic and period-three branches must have moments \(5/36,5/18,5/18\).

correctness.rationale: Integrating each coordinate equation produces three exact finite-time identities in the three time-averaged squares. Boundedness sends the endpoint terms divided by T to zero. The coefficient determinant is -b1(a1 c2+a2 c1), nonzero for the stated positive parameters, so the limiting moments are uniquely forced. The same equations follow for compact invariant measures and periodic orbits. Exact rational replay checks the nominal and c1=13/5 specializations.

value.rationale: The source's central phenomena are chaotic, periodic, and coexisting bounded states of an unusually sparse quadratic-only flow. The new law shows that every such bounded state, despite differing topology and temporal behavior, is confined to one exact coordinate-wise RMS vector, and it gives an exact numerical invariant for the paper's showcased chaotic/period-3 coexistence. This is a structural, model-wide constraint useful for validating simulations and comparing branches, not an arbitrary parameter slice or a recomputation of a published table.
